reason: The vertical scrollHeight test is not evidence of vertical glyph clipping: all four pairs retain their radicals, outer and inner fraction bars, powers, and applicable subscript. However, the desktop equation pair independently shows two reference-only antialiased pixels belonging to the initial tau's upper-left terminal, immediately outside the original .nb horizontal clip edge. The verdict uses any actual glyph-ink loss as clipping and does not claim impaired formula recognition.

recommendation.affectedOriginalDescription: If later repair is authorized, investigate only the initial tau's horizontal ink clearance in desktop equation 8.1. Do not rewrite the mathematics or declare the radicals, fractions, or subscripts defective. No repair was attempted.
recommendation.geometryGateAdvice: Keep scrollHeight excess as a diagnostic trigger, not a sufficient glyph-clipping verdict. Do not simply raise clientHeight tolerance or permit all differences under a pixel-count threshold: those policies would hide the actual two-pixel tau fringe found here.
proposedReplacementCriterionForLaterAuth: First bind an independently derived expected content/formula inventory from the authoritative edition to the current HTML. Fail missing, extra, malformed, or semantically mismatched formula content, render-error fallback, or absent visible formula output. An unclipped screenshot of the same deficient DOM is not a completeness oracle.

For each expected formula and each required display width, compare the original visible mathematical ink with a matched-position, matched-font, layout-unchanged unclipped reference whose mathematical content matches that inventory. Keep the full formula ink footprint in evidence and verify original and reference geometry has not moved; otherwise HOLD.

Fail any reference formula-ink sample absent or reduced in the original because of a clip boundary, including SVG radical paint, fraction-rule paint, glyphs, powers, subscripts, and antialiased edge samples. Use no arbitrary two-pixel or low-contrast exemption. For the supplied RGB evidence, the two white-to-gray changes at desktop crop (11,43) and (11,44) are such losses; the other three pairs have none.

Do not use text-leaf boxes alone: they omit radical SVG paths and fraction borders and can include invisible layout helpers. Distinguish crop boundaries and neighboring prose from actual formula clip edges.

A scroll-geometry anomaly with matched inventory, complete visible ink, and zero clip-attributable paint loss is a geometry false positive for clipping only. Other card-display checks and any prior failed receipt remain separate and cannot become PASS through this diagnosis.
recommendation.verificationLimit: The proposed criterion is not implemented or replay-tested here. The three pixel-identical pairs validate only the no-paint-loss distinction for these crops, not a universal gate, missing-content acceptance, or full-card PASS.
